transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. I guess I'm here because... well, I just feel worn out almost every day. It's like, even if I get a full night of sleep, I still wake up dragging. My head, my body, everything just feels heavy when I have to get up for my cashier shift. It's just been really hard to shake this tired feeling.
Besides feeling tired and worn out, how has your mood been lately? Have you been feeling sad, empty, or down?
No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or down. I mean... I don't feel empty or anything like that. My mood is mostly okay, I guess. It's really just the being worn out all the time that's getting to me.
Besides the fatigue, have you noticed any other changes in your body recently — like changes in your weight, feeling unusually hot or cold, or your heart racing?

No, not really. My weight is pretty much the same as always. I haven't been feeling too hot or cold, either. And my heart... no, it hasn't been racing or anything like that. It's really just the tiredness that's bothering me.
When you sleep for a full night, do you feel like you're actually getting good, deep sleep, or does it feel like you're not sleeping well even though you're in bed for 8 hours?

Well, it definitely doesn't feel like good, deep sleep. I mean, most nights I get into bed feeling really tired, but then I just lie there. My mind starts going over the bills, my work schedule at the store, or just wondering if everyone at home is okay. And then... even when I do finally fall asleep, I wake up feeling like I never really settled down.
During the day, do you find yourself feeling so sleepy that you struggle to stay awake, or do you just feel tired and low on energy?

I don't really struggle to stay awake, like I'm not falling asleep at the register or anything. It's more that I just feel... drained. Like I'm running on empty all day, just tired and low on energy, but not actually sleepy enough to nod off.
How long have you been experiencing this fatigue and the difficulty with sleep? Has it been going on for a few weeks, a few months, or longer?
It's been longer than a few months. I'd say... probably about a year and three months now. That's right around the time our older relative moved in with us, and it's just been going on since then.
When you finally do fall asleep at night, do you wake up multiple times during the night, or is it more that you have trouble falling asleep in the first place?

I guess it's a bit of both, really. I definitely have trouble falling asleep first, like I said, with my mind just racing. But then... yeah, once I do get to sleep, I don't stay asleep. I probably wake up two or three times a night. Sometimes I just roll over and go back to sleep, but other times I'm up for a while again, just thinking.

When you're not at work, are there things you normally enjoy doing — like hobbies, spending time with friends or family, or activities you used to like — and are you still interested in doing those things, or has that changed?

No, that hasn't really changed. I still like doing my normal stuff. I mean, I enjoy watching the game on the weekends, hanging out with a few buddies... I'm still interested in all of that. I might be a little tired when I go out, but yeah, I definitely still want to do the things I usually enjoy.
Have you tried anything to help you sleep better at night — like adjusting your bedtime routine, avoiding caffeine, or anything else? If so, did any of those things help with how rested you feel?

I haven't really tried much, to be honest. I mean, I don't drink coffee right before bed or anything, but I haven't set up a special routine or tried any sleep aids. I usually just watch TV until I feel tired, but like I said, my mind just keeps going anyway. So, no, I haven't really found anything that helps me feel more rested.

Besides feeling tired and low on energy during the day, has this lack of sleep been causing you significant problems with your work, relationships, or mood — like making it hard to concentrate at the store, getting into conflicts with people at home, or affecting your mood?

Yeah, it has a little bit. At work, um, I've noticed I'm having to double-check my cash drawer way more often. I keep making these small mistakes, probably just from not focusing well. And outside of work... well, I've actually cut back on volunteering at the local food pantry lately. I just don't feel like I can keep up with everything right now when my head's like this.

If you were able to get a full night of truly deep, uninterrupted sleep — where you fell asleep easily and stayed asleep all night — do you think you'd feel rested and energized the next day, or do you think you'd still feel tired and drained even after good sleep?

I'm honestly not sure. I haven't had a night like that in a while, so it's hard to say. I'd like to think I'd feel better and have more energy if I could just sleep through the night, but... I don't know for a fact. I guess I'd have to actually get a good night's sleep to find out.

Have you had any recent medical checkups or blood work done? I'm wondering if a doctor has checked things like your thyroid, vitamin levels, or blood count to rule out any physical health issues that could be causing this fatigue.
No, I haven't had any blood work or checkups recently. I haven't been to a regular doctor in a while, actually. So, no, nobody has checked my thyroid or anything like that.
Have you noticed any changes like your skin becoming drier, your hair falling out more than usual, feeling constipated, or having trouble with your bowels?
No, I haven't noticed anything like that. My skin and hair seem pretty normal to me. And, uh, no issues with being constipated or anything like that. Everything's just the usual in that department.
Have you noticed any changes in how you feel when it's cold outside — like feeling colder than other people around you, or needing extra blankets or layers even when others seem comfortable?

No, not really. I mean, I get cold when it's actually cold out, obviously, but... not more than anyone else, I don't think. I haven't needed to pile on extra blankets or anything like that. Just the normal amount of layers for whatever the weather is.

When you think about your fatigue and low energy — the way you feel drained all day — do you think that's mainly because you're not sleeping well, or do you feel like even if you somehow got perfect sleep, you'd still wake up feeling exhausted and worn out?

I think it's mostly because I'm just not sleeping well. Most nights, I get in bed and I'm really tired, but then I just lie there. I start going over the bills, my work schedule, wondering if everyone at home is doing okay... it just keeps going. And then, even when I do manage to fall asleep, I wake up feeling like I never really settled down. So, yeah, I think it's just that I'm not getting any actual rest.

patient.answer: I'm honestly not sure. I haven't had a night like that in a while, so it's hard to say. I'd like to think I'd feel better and have more energy if I could just sleep through the night, but... I don't know for a fact. I guess I'd have to actually get a good night's sleep to find out.

inference.note: E03.9 (hypothyroidism) ruled out - patient denies cold intolerance, skin/hair changes, constipation, and other hypothyroid symptoms. Remains between insomnia with non-restorative sleep (F51.01) and other fatigue (R53.83), though insomnia is more likely given clear sleep maintenance and onset difficulties.

target_item.name: Sleep_Disturbance
target_item.manifestation: Most nights I get in bed tired, but then I lie there going over bills, my work schedule, and whether everyone at home is okay, and even when I do sleep I wake up feeling like I never really settled down.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking if the fatigue is caused by not sleeping well or if the exhaustion persists despite perfect sleep, which relates to my sleep quality and quantity.

patient.answer: I think it's mostly because I'm just not sleeping well. Most nights, I get in bed and I'm really tired, but then I just lie there. I start going over the bills, my work schedule, wondering if everyone at home is doing okay... it just keeps going. And then, even when I do manage to fall asleep, I wake up feeling like I never really settled down. So, yeah, I think it's just that I'm not getting any actual rest.

inference.note: Ruled out R53.83 (unspecified fatigue). Patient's fatigue is directly attributable to insomnia with multiple night awakenings and initial sleep onset difficulty lasting 15 months. The fatigue is secondary to the sleep disorder, not a primary condition. Patient denies depressed mood, anhedonia, and has no medical symptoms suggesting organic causes (thyroid, anemia, etc.). This is clearly Insomnia Disorder, Non-Restorative Sleep (F51.01).

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with chronic insomnia (>1 year duration) characterized by difficulty falling asleep due to racing thoughts about bills, work schedule, and family concerns, plus multiple nighttime awakenings (2-3 times/night). The insomnia is clearly linked to a psychosocial stressor (relative moving in ~15 months ago). Patient explicitly attributes daytime fatigue to poor sleep quality rather than primary depression or anxiety disorder. No depressed mood, anhedonia, or anxiety symptoms reported. No medical causes identified (no thyroid symptoms, weight changes, temperature sensitivity, or other systemic signs). Functional impairment present (concentration difficulties at work, reduced volunteering). Patient believes good sleep would resolve fatigue, suggesting primary sleep disorder rather than depression with insomnia.
